label: rejected

evidence.V1: Bare flared trunk with upswept branches reads as a dead tree in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view shows a clear star of limbs. Recognisable at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Big trunk, medium 5 branches, small twigs, grain stripes and an end-grain cap on the snapped top: clear hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Stylised, but the limbs are smooth uniform horn/tusk shapes with pointed tan tips, and one lower limb hooks back toward the trunk like a claw; reads more antler than wood, only partly convincing.
evidence.V4: Trunk bark grooves are soft, but branch tips are needle-sharp points and branch-to-trunk junctions are hard, unblended intersections; inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Fork close-up shows branches as separate tubes jammed into the trunk with hard seams and a visible blunt branch end (dark hooked stub on the left limb); roots close-up shows a jagged folded notch on the left side of the root flare.
evidence.V6: Bark brown in 2-3 values (body, groove, light tips/end-grain); disciplined, and the ash/birch colourways stay within one hue.
evidence.V7: 1368 tris vs tree target 2000 (ceiling 5000): under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and kit palette, but branches are not fused smooth shells as the nature kit specifies, and the needle tips clash with the soft kit look; minor mismatch.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct.

evidence.V1: Bare trunk with upswept branches reads as a dead tree in front, three-quarter and silhouette, but the top view is a spiky star of tusks, and a visible branch-junction failure (see V3/V5) caps this at 1.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: tapered trunk with root flare, five medium branches, small side twigs.
evidence.V3: Branches are uniform smooth curved horns with pale pointed tips, reading more like antlers/tusks than gnarled dead wood; one branch butt hooks out of the trunk side (crown and fork close-ups) instead of fusing in, a visible junction failure.
evidence.V4: Trunk uses hard flat bark-stripe facets and a sharp root fin, while branches are soft smooth tubes with hard colour bands at the tips; edge language is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-ups show a curled branch-end stub sitting on the trunk surface (fork/crown studio), a thin jagged sliver along the left root flare (roots studio), and an abrupt seam where each branch meets the trunk with no fillet.
evidence.V6: One bark hue in 3 values (stripes) plus pale tip accent; ash and birch colourways keep the same discipline.
evidence.V7: 1368 tris vs tree target 2000 - under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material and bark palette are right, but branches are separate tubes pushed into the trunk rather than fused smooth shells, and the faceted stripe trunk differs from the smooth-shell organic standard.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Front, 3/4 and silhouette read as a bare dead tree, but a visible seating failure (branch butt ends protruding from the trunk surface, see V5) caps this at 1; top view is a clear star of limbs.
evidence.V2: Big tapered trunk and medium curved limbs read, small tier is only 3 thin twig spikes and pale tips; limbs are near-identical horn shapes so hierarchy is only partly there.
evidence.V3: Ribbed flared trunk is nicely stylised, but the limbs are uniform smooth horn/antler curves with needle tips rather than gnarled branches; capped at 1 by the seating failure anyway.
evidence.V4: Trunk has sharp-edged vertical ribs and a jagged flare, while branches are soft smooth tubes with hard flat butt ends; edge treatment is inconsistent between parts.
evidence.V5: Branch joints are not fused: in the fork close-up the right limb's flat butt end sticks out past the trunk silhouette and the upper-left limb shows a hooked stub with a dark concave end; the roots close-up shows a jagged notch crease on the left side of the trunk flare.
evidence.V6: Bark brown in 3 values (dark rib grooves, mid bark, pale tips/heartwood cap); birch and ash colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material and bark palette fit, but the kit expects fused smooth organic shells; here limbs are separate tubes with visible butt ends, a mismatch.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, SmoothPlastic, MeshPart.Color white, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: Hard unblended seams where branches enter the trunk
Visible blunt branch stub on the left lower limb at the fork
Jagged folded notch on the left side of the root flare
Branch butt hooks out of the trunk side as a visible curled stub (DeadTree_01_close_fork_studio.png, DeadTree_01_close_crown_studio.png)
Thin jagged fin/sliver on the left edge of the root flare (DeadTree_01_close_roots_studio.png)
Hard unfilleted seams where branches enter the trunk
Branch butt end protruding from the trunk side at the lower-right limb (fork close-up)
Hooked stub with dark concave end at the upper-left limb joint (crown and fork close-ups)
Jagged notch crease on the left side of the trunk flare (roots close-up)
top_fixes: Fuse branches into the trunk (union/remesh or a flared collar at each junction) so joins are smooth shells
Round off the needle tips into blunt broken-off stubs and add slight kinks so limbs read as wood, not horns
Clean the root-flare notch and give the flare 3-4 distinct root buttresses
Bury every branch butt fully inside the trunk (or fuse with a fillet) so no branch end shows outside
Fix the root-flare sliver and give the flare 3-4 distinct root lobes
Make branches gnarled: vary thickness, add kinks and taper, drop the uniform horn curve and pale tip bands
Fuse limbs into the trunk (boolean union / bridge with a collar) and bury or remove the visible butt ends
Fix the trunk-flare notch on the left side of the base
Make limbs gnarlier and varied (kinks, forks, different thickness) instead of identical horn curves, and add a few more twigs for the small tier
Soften the trunk rib edges to match the branches' edge treatment
